context: Measure the real Pages response and cache behavior first, then run a controlled N-to-N+1 redeploy/cache transition, evaluate meta versus response-header CSP against GitHub Pages constraints, define a privacy-preserving first-party synthetic check and error budget, and inspect print/200-percent-zoom/reduced-motion behavior. Record conscious acceptances with owner and review date; implement only controls justified by measured failure or an approved operational requirement.
description: The adversarial review did not reproduce a CSP exploit, mixed-version cache failure, print/zoom defect, or observability outage. It did establish that the Explorer is not deployed, uses a fixed results.duckdb URL, relies on a meta CSP because Pages exposes limited response-header control, and has no client telemetry or production synthetic monitor. Preserve those as explicit post-launch validation/decision work rather than either inventing defects or letting the dimensions disappear.

anti_patterns.dont: add Sentry, analytics, or session replay merely because no telemetry exists
anti_patterns.instead: start with first-party synthetic route/snapshot checks and make any client telemetry a separate approved decision
anti_patterns.why: the static app's privacy posture may be more valuable than detailed client traces

anti_patterns.dont: append a random cache-busting query on every page load
anti_patterns.instead: test content-addressed or deployment-versioned URLs with bounded retention and rollback
anti_patterns.why: that defeats browser/CDN caching and range-read performance

anti_patterns.dont: claim CSP failure solely because GitHub Pages lacks a response header
anti_patterns.instead: test effective directives, document Pages constraints, and tighten only with a compatible delivery mechanism
anti_patterns.why: the application already carries an enforceable meta policy and no exploit was reproduced

anti_patterns.dont: treat a screenshot at one viewport as print or zoom validation
anti_patterns.instead: exercise print media plus 200-percent zoom with measurable overflow and content-reachability assertions
anti_patterns.why: pagination, clipping, focus, and horizontal overflow differ across media and scale

preserves.behavior: A newer/older read-model mismatch continues to use the explicit remediation path rather than rendering partial data.
Cache changes preserve HTTP range-read efficiency and do not force full 34 MB-class WASM/database refetches on every navigation.
Meta CSP remains active unless an equal-or-stronger enforceable response policy replaces it.
No third-party analytics, session replay, or remote error payload is introduced without a separate privacy and data-retention decision.
Print, zoom, reduced-motion, and high-contrast checks report observed behavior without claiming full assistive-technology certification.
Synthetic monitoring records route/status/version/timing only and never bundle content, query text, comparison IDs, or user navigation.

prior_art.concept: Place any first-party post-deploy synthetic check beside the single authoritative Pages deployment.
Measure and document the existing meta CSP before choosing any replacement or tightening.
Extend the existing fixed snapshot URL and read-model mismatch handling only if the redeploy drill proves a cache/version hazard.
Reuse existing reduced-motion and high-contrast media queries for operational visual checks.

verifications.description: Live route and snapshot headers can be inspected
verifications.expected: Both live requests succeed after launch and expose the headers needed for a cache/range policy decision.

verifications.command: cd results-explorer && npx playwright test --project=chromium --workers=1 e2e/capability
verifications.description: Capability tests cover cache transition and non-default media
verifications.expected: Cache/version, range, print, zoom, reduced-motion, and high-contrast capability checks pass or produce separately owned concrete defects.
Post-deploy synthetic monitoring, privacy boundaries, and deployment ordering are mechanically guarded where implemented.

work_units.notes: Capture HTML, JS, WASM, DuckDB, bundle, and 404 response status/headers; cache-control/age/etag; range support; effective CSP; service-worker absence/presence; read-model version; console errors; and current monitoring. Distinguish browser cache, CDN cache, and application state.
work_units.summary: Measure live response headers, cache keys, range behavior, CSP, and error surfaces

work_units.notes: Load deployment N, retain HTML/JS/DB cache combinations, deploy a compatible test N+1, and exercise old HTML/new DB and new HTML/old DB combinations under cache-disabled and normal-cache modes. Verify fail-closed remediation, rollback, range budget, and eventual convergence before selecting versioned URLs or accepting current max-age.
work_units.summary: Run a controlled mixed-cache N-to-N+1 redeploy drill

work_units.notes: Test effective meta CSP including inline and wasm requirements, document which response headers Pages can control, and threat-model script/data exfiltration. Define a first-party synthetic check for /results, direct route, DB range, model version, and privacy gate with alert owner/SLO. Any client telemetry proposal requires a separate privacy decision.
work_units.summary: Decide CSP and privacy-preserving observability controls

work_units.notes: Inspect Home, benchmark/platform, detail, compare, and query routes. Assert primary content remains reachable, no page-level horizontal overflow at 200 percent, interactive controls retain names/focus, nonessential animation stops, and print does not expose clipped or misleading rankings. File concrete defects separately.
work_units.summary: Exercise print, 200-percent zoom, reduced motion, and high contrast

work_units.notes: Update the QA/runbook with measured headers/cache behavior, effective CSP, synthetic monitor and alert owner, accepted risks with expiry/review date, redeploy/rollback drill evidence, and print/zoom outcomes. No defect-free claim is inferred from missing telemetry.
work_units.summary: Record the operational baseline, decisions, owners, and review dates
